0.0.n: Used here to begin presenting the item.

0.2.n: A polite way to refer to the item being shown.

0.3.n: Adds politeness while identifying the item.

0.4.n: Invites the listener to follow along with the introduction.

0.7.n: Part of the game's English name, Betrayal at House on the Hill.

0.9.n: An English location word within the game's name.

0.11.n: Part of the game's English name, not a separate Japanese word.

0.13.n: An English location word within the game's name.

0.15.n: The English article belonging to Hill within the game's name.

0.17.n: The final word of the game's English name.

0.19.n: Links the game's name to 拡張セット, identifying which game the expansion belongs to.

0.20.n: Part of a polite filler, ですね, inserted while the speaker continues the description.

0.21.n: Softens the pause after の; the description resumes with 拡張セット.

0.23.n: Combines with セット to describe an add-on to the game.

0.24.n: An English loanword used with 拡張 for a game expansion.

0.26.n: Part of the expansion's English name, Widow's Walk.

0.28.n: This token is the s in English 's, attached to Widow within the expansion's name.

0.30.n: Part of the expansion's name; a widow's walk is a rooftop platform.

0.32.n: Politely completes the identification of the expansion.

0.33.n: Adds a friendly, conversational finish to the introduction.

1.0.n: A shortened まあ, used to ease into the explanation.

1.2.n: Politely refers to the expansion being shown.

1.3.n: Marks this item as another example of what the speaker is describing.

1.4.n: Used in the polite filler ですね before the main explanation.

1.5.n: Makes the pause after こちらも conversational and friendly.

1.7.n: Combines with に to describe how fully this qualifies as an expansion.

1.8.n: Turns 完全 into a description of degree: 完全に.

1.9.n: Modifies セット to identify this as a game add-on.

1.10.n: Together with 拡張, names the product category.

1.11.n: Marks the state described by なっていまして: being an expansion set.

1.12.n: Polite linking form of なっている, from なる; describes its status and connects to the next clause.

1.14.n: Refers back to the expansion, rather than the base game.

1.15.n: After これ, emphasizes the expansion considered separately from the base game.

1.16.n: Marks using the expansion alone as the means of playing.

1.17.n: Highlights the condition これ単体で, contrasting it with use alongside the base game.

1.18.n: An English loanword that forms a verb when followed by する.

1.19.n: Combines with プレイ to make the verb for playing a game.

1.20.n: Turns プレイする into a noun-like phrase so it can be discussed as an ability.

1.21.n: Marks プレイすること as the action whose possibility is being denied.

1.22.n: Polite negative of できる; with a verb plus ことが, expresses inability to perform that action.

2.0.n: A conversational connector that moves on to the contents.

2.2.n: Asks about the contents of the expansion.

2.3.n: Marks 何 as the thing contained inside.

2.4.n: Short for 入っている, from 入る; describes the current contents rather than an ongoing entry.

2.5.n: Marks 何が入ってる as an embedded question: what is inside.

2.6.n: Casually quotes the preceding question as the topic the speaker will answer.

2.7.n: With って and と, introduces an explanation answering the preceding question.

2.8.n: Completes っていうと, a conversational way to introduce an answer or explanation.

2.10.n: With は, identifies the essential nature of the contents.

2.11.n: Marks 基本 as the topic of the explanation.

2.12.n: Combines with に to frame the addition as straightforward.

2.13.n: Turns 単純 into a description of how to understand the contents.

2.14.n: A loanword referring to the game's playable stories or situations.

2.15.n: Links シナリオ to 増加, specifying what increases.

2.16.n: A noun describing the addition of more game scenarios.

2.17.n: Connects the noun 増加 to the explanatory んです.

2.18.n: Short for の; presents the statement as an explanation of the contents.

2.19.n: Adds politeness to the explanatory ending なんです.

2.20.n: Gently draws the listener into the explanation.

0.lit: Yes, this is it, you see: Betrayal at House on the Hill's expansion set, Widow's Walk, you see.
0.tip: The repeated ですね keeps the introduction polite and conversational, even when inserted mid-phrase.

1.lit: Well, this too is entirely an expansion set, and with this alone, playing is not possible.
1.tip: A verb followed by ことができません means you cannot do that action.

2.lit: So, if saying what is inside, the basics are simply an increase of scenarios, you see.
2.tip: かっていうと introduces a question the speaker is about to answer.
